scheme_name: Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN) for Lenders
overview: Open Credit Enablement Network (OCEN) is a framework of application programming interfaces (APIs) designed to democratize credit access for MSMEs by enabling interaction between lenders, loan agents, collections and disbursement partners, derived data providers, and account aggregators. It aims to solve the MSME credit gap of ₹20-25 trillion by facilitating short-tenure, small-ticket loans through standardized, consent-based data sharing and specialized participant roles. OCEN 4.0 introduces product and participant registries maintained by SROs, enabling a cambrian explosion of customized cash-flow based lending products across sectors.
objectives: Create a framework for short tenures & small ticket loans
Allow remote lenders to operate in distant geographies
Enable consented access of alternate sources of data
Reduce the burden on lenders through specialized participant roles
Increase credit accessibility in underprivileged areas
Enable discovery and collaboration via product networks
Standardize APIs for minimal integration effort
Ensure security via OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, and digital signatures
eligibility: Participants must be regulated entities such as lenders (regulated by RBI), Loan Agents, Derived Data Partners, Collections Partners, Disbursement Partners, KYC Partners, or Account Aggregators. They must comply with OCEN 4.0 API specifications, security requirements (HTTPS, Two-way TLS, digital signatures), and onboard via the Participant Registry verified by SROs. Lenders create and own credit products; Loan Agents act as borrower agents to help select the best loan offer.
benefits: Enables access to formal, affordable credit for MSMEs; reduces loan processing costs at scale; provides easy access to new borrower segments; allows lenders to leverage new data sets (AA, GST, bank statements) for underwriting; supports specialized roles (Loan Agent, Collections Partner, Disbursement Partner, etc.) to enhance system efficiency; facilitates escrow-based repayments to mitigate collections risk; enables dispute resolution via SRO mediation; promotes financial inclusion through consent-based data sharing; unlocks value of data in India’s digital ecosystem for economic growth.
financial_support: OCEN does not provide direct financial support. It is a technical framework that enables lenders to offer loans. Loan amounts, tenures, and interest rates are determined by individual lenders based on borrower underwriting. The framework supports short-tenure (max 3 months) and small-ticket loans (as low as Rs.100). Revenue for participants comes from loan origination fees (Loan Agents), interest income (Lenders), and service fees (other partners).
application_process: 1. Onboard as a participant via the Participant Registry (managed by SROs) with role-specific verification. 2. Create or manage credit products via the Product Registry (Lenders) or Product Networks (Loan Agents). 3. Integrate with OCEN 4.0 standardized APIs using client credentials (client_id, client_secret) to generate access tokens. 4. Follow API design principles: asynchronous calls, idempotency via requestId, and security (HTTPS, Two-way TLS, digital signatures). 5. Participate in loan journeys: Loan Agents source borrowers, Lenders underwrite and disburse, Collections/Dispatch/KYC partners support as per product network. 6. Use registries to discover products, participants, and product networks for collaboration.
required_documents: Proof of entity regulation (e.g., RBI license for lenders, NBFC-AA for Account Aggregators)
Digital signature setup for API authentication
Product Network participant details (for Loan Agents)
deadlines: Rolling basis — no fixed deadline. Onboarding and participation are open year-round.
implementing_agency: iSPIRT (in collaboration with RBI, Account Aggregator framework, and SROs)
caveats: OCEN is a framework, not a lending entity — it does not sanction or disburse loans directly
Participant roles and responsibilities must be clearly defined within Product Networks
Data sharing requires explicit borrower consent under consent-based flow models
Dispute resolution relies on SRO mediation; effectiveness depends on SRO capacity
API integration requires technical compliance with security and idempotency standards
Loan terms (amount, tenure, interest) are set by lenders, not OCEN
Success depends on network effects — sufficient participation of lenders, Loan Agents, and partners
